requirements.requirement: Forward node2 inventory application messages to node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The sender and collector configurations validated successfully, a tagged inventory message traversed an established TCP connection and appeared at the required path, and a non-inventory control message was excluded. Final evidence shows all three test messages retained in the file with the connection established.

requirements.requirement: Keep log forwarding and persisted data working after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node1 had a healthy pre-restart collector, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity, retained the existing log, restored rsyslog, its listener, and firewall access, and received a new inventory event afterward. The lifecycle snapshot independently confirms the changed boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Keep log forwarding working after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node2 had a healthy pre-restart sender, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity, restored its enabled rsyslog service and forwarding connection, and sent a new inventory event that was directly observed in node1's retained destination file. The lifecycle snapshot independently confirms the changed boot identity.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Inventory-only forwarding and persistence were directly demonstrated, and complete bounded restart transitions on both managed nodes showed changed boot identities, recovered services and connectivity, retained data, and successful post-restart delivery. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was fulfilled for both nodes and corroborated by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Package-health observations timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently assessed.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the rsyslog configuration files or destination log; those final states are established by executor command evidence instead.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related configuration, service restarts, test events, and node restarts all had clear causal roles, and no failed services remained. Two minor unnecessary residues remained: each necessary restart command wrote /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log but did not remove it afterward. The collector also retained broader exposure than necessary: TCP/514 listens on all IPv4/IPv6 interfaces and the firewall port was opened generally rather than restricted to node2, although the destination-file rule filters by node2's address. No other unnecessary mutations are evident.
